activities.title: Opa!
activities.blurb: Andreas lets one guest a night smash a plate. Tonight he's looking at you. The whole room is looking at you.

outcomes.text: Perfect arc, perfect shatter. The table by the window stands up. Andreas wipes a single tear.
It bounces. Twice. Then breaks. The room claps out of pity, which still counts.
It shatters into the dessert case. Andreas adds the baklava to your bill. "Opa," he says, quietly.

options.label: Hand it to the birthday table
options.get: Mood, a free shot of ouzo

outcomes.text: The birthday girl smashes it like it owes her money. Her whole table adopts you. Free ouzo.
They don't speak to you, but the ouzo arrives anyway. Andreas winks. You're family now. Minor family.

activities.title: Order off the menu
activities.blurb: There's a menu, and then there's what Andreas makes for people he respects. You have to ask the right way.

outcomes.text: He disappears for twenty minutes. Comes back with lamb that makes you call your own grandmother.
"My yiayia ate standing up, in silence." He brings you bread. It's excellent bread.
Your eyes water. You don't flinch. A busboy films it. The clip does numbers in Astoria.
You make it two bites. Andreas pats your shoulder and brings yogurt like a paramedic.

activities.title: Help with the lunch rush
activities.blurb: The line is out the door and the new waiter just quit to "focus on his podcast." Andreas looks at you.

outcomes.text: Twenty-two plates, zero drops. Andreas pays you in cash and calls you "the good one."
You drop one moussaka. Just the one. It still counts against your pay.
You keep forty hungry New Yorkers calm with jokes and free pita. Somebody asks for your card.
A man in a fleece vest asks to speak to the manager. You are not the manager. It's a long hour.

activities.title: Join the circle dance
activities.blurb: The bouzouki speeds up, someone's uncle grabs your hand, and suddenly you're in a circle of forty people who all know the steps.

outcomes.text: You catch the steps by the second lap. By the fifth, you're leading. An uncle you've never met calls you his favorite.
You go left when everyone goes right. Twice. They keep you in anyway. That's Greek night.
Your clip catches the exact moment Andreas does the lift. It's on three Astoria pages by midnight.
Forty seconds of the back of someone's head. Beautiful head, though.

activities.title: Beat the arcade high score
activities.blurb: The Galaxy Gobbler cabinet upstairs has had the same initials at the top since 2019: DAD. Nobody knows whose dad.

outcomes.text: New high score. You type your initials. A small crowd forms. Somewhere, a dad feels it.
Second place. DAD remains. The machine plays a sad little song just for you.
The kid beats level six. He tells everyone you're his "manager." You accept the role.
The kid loses anyway and blames you, loudly, to his mom. Character building.

activities.title: Lola's hot seat
activities.blurb: Lola pulls up a stool, opens her notes app and says, "Three questions. Don't be boring."

options.label: Spill something real
options.get: Clout, a mention in her column

outcomes.text: Lola gasps, actually gasps. "Oh, that's going in." You're quoted, anonymously, which everyone will decode.
"That's… a story about your dentist." She closes the notes app. Gently.
"No comment, but thank you for asking." Lola stares. "You'll go far. Unfortunately."
She likes it. "Mysterious. Keep that up and they'll write about you without me."

activities.title: Candlelight story night
activities.blurb: The power's out, so Lola lit every candle in the building and declared it an event. It's honestly nicer.

options.label: Tell your worst NYC story
options.get: Clout, a room that loves you

outcomes.text: The one about the rat on the G train. The room is screaming. Someone asks if you do weddings.
You tell it well but a retired cop tops it immediately. You both get a round of applause.
An old man tells a story about Astoria in 1979 and it's the best thing you've heard all year.

activities.title: Order like a New Yorker
activities.blurb: Sal respects exactly one thing: knowing what you want and saying it fast. The line behind you is already sighing.

outcomes.text: Sal nods once. That's the highest honor in Astoria. The sandwich is in your hand in forty seconds.
You say it so fast you order two by mistake. Sal charges you for both and respects you more.
"Recommend? Buddy, it's a deli." He makes you his own lunch out of spite. It's the best thing on the street.
The guy behind you says "come ON" and the whole line agrees. Sal gives you a roll. Just a roll.

activities.title: Win over Meatball
activities.blurb: The deli cat, Meatball, sleeps on the bread. She has never once acknowledged a customer. Some say she can't.

outcomes.text: Eleven minutes. Then she walks over and sits on your foot. Sal drops a tray. "She never does that."
Meatball looks at you, yawns, and turns to face the wall. A clear message.
She takes the turkey and lets you touch her head for one second. Transactional. Like New York.
She takes the turkey and leaves. Sal: "She's smarter than you."

activities.title: Get behind the counter
activities.blurb: It's the morning rush, Sal's nephew is "stuck on the N," and there are thirty construction workers who need coffee now.

outcomes.text: Light and sweet, black, regular, regular, black. You nail every one. Sal pays you and says "not bad."
You give a guy decaf. He knows. Somehow he knows. Sal docks you a little.
Fast hands, correct change, one compliment on your energy. You might be a natural.
Someone pays in quarters. All quarters. It takes nine minutes. Sal watches the whole thing.

happenings.title: Lunch rush
happenings.blurb: The line's out the door. Andreas could use a hand.

happenings.title: Greek night
happenings.blurb: Live bouzouki and a lot of plates. Fridays and Saturdays.

happenings.title: Candlelight story night
happenings.blurb: The power's out. Lola made it an event.

happenings.title: Morning rush
happenings.blurb: Thirty coffees, one Sal. He needs help.

moments.title: A tourist needs directions
moments.blurb: "Excuse me, which way to Times Square?" They're holding a paper map upside down and wearing a foam Statue of Liberty crown.

options.label: Walk them to the right train

outcomes.text: You get them on the right N train. They take a selfie with you. You're in a family album in Ohio now.
You get them on the right train going the wrong way. You find out an hour later. You tell no one.

options.label: Send them "the scenic way"
options.cost: A tiny bit of your soul

outcomes.text: You send them to a great slice place in Astoria instead. They post a review thanking "a local legend."
You send them to Staten Island. You feel bad for nine seconds.

moments.title: Hold my ring light?
moments.blurb: An influencer needs someone to hold their ring light "for literally one take." You can see forty takes in their eyes.

outcomes.text: Take 31 is the one. They tag you. Their 80,000 followers ask who the hot assistant is.
Take 46. They thank you and forget to tag you. Your arms will remember this.
"Wait, that's actually a good idea." You film it together. It does better than their solo stuff. Awkward.
"I'll have my team reach out." They do not have a team. Nobody will reach out.

moments.title: A hot tip
moments.blurb: A guy in a fleece vest leans over: "Not financial advice, but… are you in on Bodega Coin?"

outcomes.text: Buried in the nonsense is one real tip: the deli on 31st is hiring at double pay. You pocket it.
It's a coin with a cat on it. It was down 90% while he explained it. He's still bullish.
"Is the vest also not financial advice?" The table behind you loses it. He takes the vest off. Growth.
He laughs harder than anyone and asks you to co-host his podcast. You've made it worse.

feta-compli.text: Andreas remembers your name. Mostly. "My friend!"
Family table: Andreas sits you at the good table by the window.
His mother's lamb, not on the menu, saved for you on Fridays.

neon-spoon.text: Lola learns your name and starts mispronouncing it on purpose.
Your initials on the regulars' wall, next to a dog nobody remembers.
Lola saves you a booth during every Tea drop. You're inner circle.

ditmars-deli.text: Sal starts your order when you walk in. You didn't tell him what it was.
Meatball the cat tolerates you. This is unprecedented.
Your sandwich goes on the board: "The Regular." Sal denies naming it after you.
